info.title: Omnibus API
info.description: The REST API behind every Omnibus client. The web app, the iOS app and the MCP server all use it, and a new client can too. ## Signing in `POST /api/auth/login` opens a session. Set `client_kind` to `ios`, `android` or `bearer` and the token comes back in the response body; send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer `. Leave `client_kind` out and the server sets a session cookie instead, which is what a browser wants. An API token (`omni_…`, from `POST /api/auth/api-tokens`) works anywhere a session token does, and suits scripts. Some media, such as covers, audio parts and book files, gets loaded straight into an `` or `

get.description:
Answers without a session, so a client can probe a server address before signing in.
`time` lets a client measure its clock's offset before it stamps progress writes.

post.description:
Replaces your profile picture. The server checks the bytes are a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP
image and stores the type it finds, not the one sent.

schema.description: Describes the multipart form `POST /api/account/avatar` takes: one image part.

avatar.description:
A JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image of at most 10 MiB, sent with an `image/*` content type.
SVG is refused.

400.description: The form has no `avatar` part, or the part isn't an `image/*` type, is SVG, or is larger than 10 MiB.

415.description: The bytes aren't a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image.

delete.description:
Deletes your profile picture, so clients show your initials instead. Succeeds when you
have no avatar too.

post.description:
Chooses whether a book's detail page stops at each section as you scroll. Read back as
`book_detail_scroll_stops` on `GET /api/auth/me`.

Replaces the list of formats your library view leaves out. Clients pass the saved list,
read back as `hidden_formats` on `GET /api/auth/me`, as the listing's `exclude_formats`.

422.description: A format name isn't 1 to 16 letters or digits, or the list has more than 32; the body says which.

post.description:
Sets or clears the address `POST /api/kindle/send` emails books to. Read back as
`kindle_email` on `GET /api/auth/me`.

422.description: The address doesn't look like an email address, or is over 320 bytes.

post.description:
Sets or clears the name other readers see on your journal entries, ratings and shared
stats. With no display name, your username shows instead.

422.description: The name is longer than 64 characters or has a control character.

post.description:
Chooses whether other readers on this server can see your reading stats. Read back as
`share_stats` on `GET /api/auth/me`.

Chooses whether your library grid folds each series into one tile. Read back as
`stack_series` on `GET /api/auth/me`.

delete.description:
Deletes a device registration, whoever it belongs to, and signs out every session on
it. Needs an admin account.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The device's id, from the devices listing.

204.description: The device and its sessions are gone.

get.description:
One snapshot of the library index, the background task queue, the search index, disk
use and the most recent errors. Poll it to keep a view current. Needs an admin account.

delete.description:
Signs one session out, whoever it belongs to. You can't revoke the session you sent
this request with; sign out instead. Needs an admin account.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The session's id, from the sessions listing.

400.description: That is the session this request came with.

404.description: No live session has that id.

get.description:
Every account on the server, up to 1000, with its permissions and whether it is locked
out. Needs an admin account.

post.description:
Makes an account with the permissions you give it, whether or not registration is open.
Needs an admin account.

409.description: That username is taken, ignoring case.

422.description: The username or password breaks a rule; the body says which.

delete.description:
Deletes the account and everything that is only theirs: progress, highlights, journal
entries, shelves and sessions. Books they added stay in the library. This can't be
undone. Needs an admin account.

409.description: The user is the last admin.

get.description:
The apps the user has signed in from, each registered as a device. An unknown user id
lists nothing. Needs an admin account.

200.description: The user's devices, most recently seen first.

post.description:
Sets a new password without asking for the old one, and signs the user out everywhere.
Needs an admin account.

204.description: The password is changed and the user's sessions are revoked.

422.description: The password breaks a rule; the body says which.

patch.description: Replaces all four permission flags. Needs an admin account.

409.description: The user is the last admin, and the change would take admin away.

get.description:
The user's live sign-ins, on browsers and apps. `is_current` is always `false` here,
even for your own session. An unknown user id lists nothing. Needs an admin account.

post.description:
Ends a lockout from too many wrong passwords, so the user can sign in again now.
Succeeds when the user isn't locked too. Needs an admin account.

get.description:
Names, dates and the last four characters of each live token. A token's secret is shown
only once, when it is created.

post.description:
Makes a long-lived token that authenticates as you, for scripts and integrations. Copy
`secret` from the response: the server keeps only a hash of it and can't show it again.

200.description: The new token, with its secret.

400.description: The name is empty or too long.

delete.description: The token stops working at once.

404.description: You have no live token with that id.

400.description: The name is empty or too long.

404.description: You have no live token with that id.

post.description:
Checks the username and password and opens a session. Set `client_kind` to `ios`,
`android` or `bearer` to get the token in the body, for an `Authorization: Bearer`
header; without it the session arrives as a cookie. Send `device_name` as well and the
session is listed under that name.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie, unless `client_kind` asked for a token.

400.description: `device_name` or `client_version` is too long or holds control characters.

429.description: Too many wrong passwords: the account is locked for the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.

post.description:
Ends the session the request carries and clears the session cookie. Signing out of a
session that has already ended still succeeds.

get.description: The account the request's session belongs to: its permissions and preferences.

401.description: The request has no live session.

post.description:
Creates a user and signs them in, exactly as `POST /api/auth/login` does. The first
account on a new server becomes its admin. After that, registration works only while an
admin keeps it open; `GET /api/auth/registration` says whether it is.

200.description: The account exists and is signed in.

Set-Cookie.description: The session cookie, unless `client_kind` asked for a token.

400.description: The username or password breaks a rule; the body says which.

get.description:
Whether `POST /api/auth/register` will accept a new account. An admin opens and closes
registration with `POST /api/settings/registration`.

Every live session on your account. The one making this request has `is_current` set,
since it can't be ended from here.

delete.description:
Signs that session out wherever it is. To end the session making this request, use
`POST /api/auth/logout`.

400.description: That is the session making this request.

404.description: You have no live session with that id.

get.description:
Every author with a book in the library, surname first, each with a book count, an
accent color and whether a photo is cached. Stops at 10,000 authors.

get.summary: List your progress through each author
get.description:
For each author whose books you have opened or marked: how many you have finished, how
many you are reading, and when you last read one. Authors you haven't started are left
out.

200.description: Your progress, one row per author.

post.description:
Drops every photo found at Open Library and searches again for every author, in the
background. Uploaded photos are kept. Answers at once, before the work starts. Needs
an admin account.

get.description:
One author and all their books. `reading` holds your own status and position on each
of those books you have opened or marked. Opening an author with no photo yet starts a
search for one in the background.

The author's profile photo. When none is cached, the server looks for one at Open
Library in the background, so a later request may find it. Once Open Library has had
none, the author stays without a photo until an admin deletes the photo record or
scans again.

404.description: The author has no photo, or no author has that id.

put.description:
Sets the author's photo from an uploaded image. An uploaded photo wins over one found
at Open Library, and a scan doesn't replace it. Needs an admin account.

photo.description:
The photo: a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image of 10 MiB or less, sent with an
`image/*` content type. SVG is refused.

400.description: The form has no `photo` part, or the part's content type isn't `image/*`, is SVG, or the image is larger than 10 MiB.

415.description: The bytes aren't a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image.

delete.description:
Drops the author's photo, uploaded or found, and any record that Open Library had
none. The next request for the photo starts a fresh search. Succeeds when there is no
photo, and for an unknown id. Needs an admin account.

post.summary: Search Open Library for an author's photo
post.description:
Drops a photo found earlier, or the record that Open Library had none, and asks Open
Library again, answering once it has. `resolved` says whether a photo was found. An
uploaded photo is kept as it is, and the answer is `resolved: true`. Needs an admin
account.

200.description: Whether the author has a photo now.

put.summary: Set an author's photo from a URL
put.description:
Downloads the image at `url` and saves it as the author's photo, the same as an
upload: it wins over Open Library, and a scan doesn't replace it. The server fetches
the URL itself, refuses addresses inside its own network, and doesn't follow
redirects. Needs an admin account.

400.description: `url` is empty, longer than 2048 bytes, not `http` or `https`, or points inside the server's network, or what it serves isn't a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image of 10 MiB or less; the body says which.

post.description:
Folds the source book into the target: the target takes the source's files, links,
identifiers and every reader's progress, highlights and other data, and the source
book disappears. `POST /api/books/merge/undo` with the returned `merge_log_id` reverses
it. Needs an admin account.

404.description: No book has the source or target uuid; the body says which.

422.description: The source and target are the same book.

get.description:
Searches the ebook and audiobook libraries for a book to merge another into, and returns
up to 20 matches. Needs an admin account.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Free text, optionally with `author:`, `series:`, `tag:` and `genre:` terms. At most
1024 bytes.

400.description: `q` is missing or over 1024 bytes.

post.description:
Splits a merged book back into the two it was made from, and returns the restored
source book's uuid. Needs an admin account.

409.description: The merge is already undone, or something changed since that undo can't settle, such as a later merge into the same book; the body says what.

post.summary: Delete a book's files or copies
post.description:
Deletes the listed files from disk and the listed physical copies from the collection.
When nothing of the book is left, the book goes too, with every reader's data for it:
the `impact` that `GET /api/books/{uuid}/deletion-manifest` counts. This can't be undone.
Needs an admin account.

200.description: What was deleted, and whether the book went with it.

422.description: A file or copy id isn't one of this book's; the body says which.

get.description:
What `POST /api/books/{uuid}/delete-files` can delete for this book, its files and
physical copies, and how much reader data deleting all of them would take with the
book. Needs an admin account.

200.description: The book's files and copies, and the reader data at stake.

get.description: The full-size cover image, in the format it was stored in.

304.description: The cover is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`.

404.description: No book has that uuid, or the book has no cover.

get.description:
The library's books, ebooks and audiobooks together. Without paging parameters the
response is the whole library, capped at 50,000 books: `X-Total-Count` holds the true
total, and `X-Total-Cap` appears when the cap cut the list short. Set `sort`, `dir`,
`limit` or `cursor` to page through it instead, following `X-Next-Cursor`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The order to list books in.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description:
Where the page starts: the previous page's `X-Next-Cursor`. Needs `sort` and `dir`,
set as they were for that page.

parameters.name: formats
parameters.description:
Comma-separated formats to include, such as `m4b,mp3`. Older clients send this;
newer ones put a `format` clause in `filter`.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Filter clauses as a percent-encoded JSON array, such as
`[{"field":"format","mode":"include","values":["epub"]}]`. A clause matches a book
when any of its values does, and a book must match every clause. Up to 16 clauses
of up to 64 values each.

parameters.name: exclude_formats
parameters.description:
Comma-separated formats to leave out, such as `cbz`: the formats the user hides
from their library view.

parameters.name: stack_series
parameters.description:
Fold each series of two or more books into one row and list the series in `stacks`.
`X-Total-Count` still counts books. Applies to a paged request only.

parameters.name: omit_description
parameters.description: Leave each book's description out, for a lighter page. Applies to a paged request only.

200.description: A page of books, or the whole library.

X-Hidden-Count.description: How many books `exclude_formats` left out. Sent on the first page only.

X-Next-Cursor.description: The `cursor` for the next page. Absent on the last page, and when the request wasn't paged.

X-Total-Cap.description: The cap, sent when it cut an unpaged response short.

400.description: A `cursor` came without `sort` and `dir`, or a `cursor` or `filter` is malformed.

get.description: One book's full record.

Books that Hardcover's curated lists pair with this one, for a "readers also enjoyed"
strip. `status` is `not_configured` when the server has no Hardcover key, `pending`
while the server fetches them in the background (ask again shortly), or `ready` with
the items, which may be empty. Results are kept for 30 days, then refreshed.

200.description: The suggestions, or why there are none yet.

post.description:
Asks one provider for a summary of the book and returns its text, or `null` when that
provider has none (try the next source from `GET /api/summary/sources`). An unknown
uuid also answers `null`. Nothing is saved. A provider that can't be reached is a 500.
Needs the edit permission.

Rebuilds the index book search reads from the library's current records, and answers
when it is done. Use it when search results don't match the library. Needs an admin
account.

get.description:
Every genre assigned to a book, with the number of books carrying it, most-used
first. Stops at the 500 most-used genres.

get.summary: Get the Google Books key's status
get.description:
Whether a Google Books API key is set, where it comes from, and a masked preview. The
key itself is never returned. Needs an admin account.

post.description:
Saves the server-wide Google Books API key, or clears it when `key` is `null`, absent
or blank. With a key, ISBN lookups ask Google Books first; without one, Open Library.
Clearing the saved key falls back to the server's `GOOGLE_BOOKS_API_KEY` environment
variable, when that is set. Needs an admin account.

422.description: The key is longer than 512 bytes.

get.description:
Whether a Hardcover API key is set, where it comes from, and a masked preview. The key
itself is never returned. Needs an admin account.

post.description:
Saves the server-wide Hardcover API token, or clears it when `key` is `null`, absent or
blank. The key turns on book suggestions, makes Hardcover the first source for
summaries, and adds it as the last source for ISBN lookups. Clearing the saved key
falls back to the server's `HARDCOVER_API_KEY` environment variable, when that is set.
Needs an admin account.

422.description: The key is longer than 2048 bytes.

post.summary: Send a book to your Kindle
post.description:
Queues an email of the book's EPUB, or its PDF when it has no EPUB, to your Kindle
address, and answers before it goes out. Poll `GET /api/kindle/send/status` with the
`task_id` to learn whether it was sent. A file over 50 MB fails there, not here.

409.description: The server has no email delivery set up.

422.description: `book_uuid` is longer than 64 bytes, or you have no Kindle address set.

get.description:
Whether a send from `POST /api/kindle/send` is still going, went out, or failed. Poll
about once a second: a finished send is forgotten 10 seconds after it ends.

404.description: No send of yours has that `task_id`, or it ended more than 10 seconds ago.

post.description:
Fetches one search candidate again from the provider that offered it, which returns
more than the search did. Answers `null` when the provider no longer knows the
candidate. Send the candidate's `isbn13` when it has one: it names the exact printing.
Needs the edit permission.

400.description: `provider_ref` is blank or longer than 256 bytes, or `isbn13` is longer than 32 characters.

502.description: The provider couldn't be reached, or it rate-limited the server recently and is still cooling down.

post.description:
Asks the metadata providers, all of them or those in `providers`, for editions that
match, and returns every candidate labelled with the provider it came from. Each
provider also gets a row in `sources`: a provider that fails or is skipped says so
there, and the search still succeeds. Send `title`, `author` and `isbn` when you have
them; `query` alone is searched as a title. Needs the edit permission.

200.description: The candidates and each provider's status.

400.description: Every field is blank, a field is too long, or `providers` is an empty list; the body says which.

get.description:
Every external metadata provider the server knows: its name, whether it needs an API
key, whether it can be asked right now, and what it can answer. No key material is
returned.

delete.description:
Deletes one physical copy, say after you sold it. The book stays, even when this was
its last copy: `DELETE /api/physical/{uuid}` removes a book with no files. Only the
reader who checked the copy in, or an admin, can remove it.

403.description: Someone else checked the copy in.

patch.description:
Replaces the copy's free-text note. A `null` or blank note clears it. Only the reader
who checked the copy in, or an admin, can change it.

400.description: The note is longer than 4096 characters.

403.description: Someone else checked the copy in.

delete.summary: Delete a book with no files
delete.description:
Deletes a book that has no digital files, with everything tied to it, such as its
physical copies, wishlist entries and ratings, for every reader. Clients offer it when
the last physical copy goes. Needs the edit permission.

409.description: The book still has digital files.

get.description:
Every physical copy of the book, whoever checked it in, oldest check-in first. An
unknown uuid has no copies, so the list is empty.

get.summary: Get your wishlist entry for a book
get.description: Your physical wishlist entry for the book, or `null` when it isn't on your wishlist.

post.summary: Add a book to your wishlist
post.description:
Adds a book the library already has to your physical wishlist. Adding it again returns
the existing entry. To wishlist a book the library doesn't have, use
`POST /api/scan/wishlist`.

delete.summary: Remove a book from your wishlist
delete.description:
Removing a book that isn't on your wishlist still succeeds. A book that exists only
because someone wanted it (no file, no physical copy, no other reader's entry) is
deleted with its last entry, and `book_deleted` tells you so.

200.description: The entry is gone; whether the book went with it.

post.description:
Scans the ebook library folder for added, changed and removed books, and answers when
the scan is done. Audiobooks aren't scanned; `POST /api/scan-library` covers both
libraries without waiting. Needs an admin account.

409.description: No ebook library path is set.

post.description:
Queues a scan of the ebook and audiobook library folders, whichever are set, and answers
without waiting for them. Needs an admin account.

Records a physical copy of a book the library already has, filed under you, and takes
the book off every reader's wishlist. `isbn` is stored as an ISBN-13, or dropped when
it isn't a valid ISBN. The answer carries the book's current uuid, which differs from
`book_uuid` when that book has been merged into another.

400.description: `book_uuid` is empty or longer than 64 bytes, `isbn` is longer than 32 characters, or `note` is longer than 4096 characters.

get.summary: Check whether a Google Books key is set
get.description:
`true` when the server has a Google Books API key, saved in settings or set in its
environment. Without one, Google Books lookups share an anonymous quota that runs out
quickly, so a client can warn that ISBN lookups may fail.

post.summary: Add a book you have only on paper
post.description:
Creates a book with no files from provider metadata, such as the `online` of a
`not_in_library` outcome, and checks in its first copy under you. The cover at
`cover_url` is downloaded now, from the known provider hosts only; when that fails,
the book has no cover.

400.description: A field of `meta` is too long, or `note` is longer than 4096 characters; the body says which.

post.description:
Looks a scanned or typed ISBN up in the library, then at the metadata providers, and
says what to offer next: `already_owned`, `on_wishlist` (yours), `in_library_unowned`,
`close_match` (a library book with the same title and author, to confirm before
writing anything), `not_in_library` or `unresolved`. Takes an ISBN-10 or ISBN-13, with
or without hyphens.

400.description: The ISBN is empty, longer than 32 characters, or not a valid ISBN.

503.description: No metadata provider could be reached.

post.description:
Matches a result from `POST /api/scan/search` against the library, as
`POST /api/scan/resolve` does for an ISBN, without asking the providers again. The
outcome is never `unresolved`.

400.description: A field of `meta` is too long; the body says which.

post.description:
Searches the metadata providers by free text, for when an ISBN resolves to
`unresolved`. Pass the result the reader picks to `POST /api/scan/resolve-meta`. An
empty list means the providers answered and none matched.

400.description: The query is blank or longer than 200 characters.

503.description: No metadata provider could be reached.

post.summary: Add a scanned book to your wishlist
post.description:
Adds a book to your physical wishlist: a library book by `book_uuid`, or one the
library doesn't have from `meta`, which creates a book with no files to hold the
entry. When both are sent, `book_uuid` wins. A book already on your wishlist stays as
it was.

200.description: The book is on your wishlist.

400.description: Neither `book_uuid` nor `meta` was sent, `book_uuid` is blank or longer than 64 bytes, or a field of `meta` is too long.

get.description:
Every series with a book in the library, by name, each with a book count, the first
book's first author and an accent color. Stops at 10,000 series.
One series and its books, in series order.

Where the ebook and audiobook libraries live, and how often the server rescans them.
Needs an admin account.

post.description:
Replaces the library settings and, when an ebook library is set, starts a rescan of it
in the background. Needs an admin account.

200.description: The settings are saved; the body is what is now set.

422.description: A library path is over 4096 bytes, or `scan_interval_hours` is below 1.

get.summary: Check whether the MCP endpoint is on
get.description: Whether the server answers MCP clients at `/mcp`. Needs an admin account.

post.summary: Turn the MCP endpoint on or off
post.description:
Chooses whether the server answers MCP clients at `/mcp`. The change applies to the
next `/mcp` request, with no restart. Needs an admin account.

Chooses whether `POST /api/auth/register` accepts new accounts. Anyone can read the
setting, signed in or not, with `GET /api/auth/registration`. Needs an admin account.

get.description:
Every shelf you can see: your own, every public shelf, and every shelf at all when you
are an admin. Each comes with its book count and up to four member uuids for a cover
mosaic.

post.description:
Creates a shelf you own. A smart shelf needs `match_mode` and at least one rule, and
takes no `book_uuids`. A hand-picked shelf takes no rules, and can start with
`book_uuids`. A `wishlist` shelf can't be created: every reader has one already.

404.description: A uuid in `book_uuids` matches no book.

409.description: You already have a shelf with that name.

422.description: The name, description, rules or `book_uuids` are invalid; the body says which.

get.summary: List the hand-picked shelves holding a book
get.description:
The ids of the hand-picked shelves you can see that hold the book, for a "which shelves
is this on" checklist. An unknown uuid is on no shelf, so the list is empty.

200.description: Ids of the shelves holding the book.

get.summary: List the smart shelves matching a book
get.description:
The ids of the smart shelves you can see whose rules match the book right now. Kept
apart from `GET /api/shelves/containing/{uuid}` because a smart shelf's membership
can't be toggled. An unknown uuid matches nothing, so the list is empty.

200.description: Ids of the smart shelves matching the book.

post.description:
Counts how many books a set of rules would match, out of how many in the library, with
a sample of up to 12 of them. Nothing is saved. Rules on your own data, such as rating
and read status, are matched against yours.

200.description: The match count, the library total and a sample.

422.description: More than 50 rules, an operator the field doesn't take, an empty value, or a value that can't be evaluated; the body says which.

get.description: One shelf's details, with its rules when it is a smart shelf.

404.description: No shelf has that id, or it is another reader's private shelf.

delete.description:
Deletes the shelf, its rules and its list of books; the books stay in the library.
Only the shelf's owner or an admin can delete it, and the Wishlist shelf can't be
deleted.

403.description: The shelf is someone else's, or it is the Wishlist shelf.

404.description: No shelf has that id, or it is another reader's private shelf.

patch.description:
Changes the fields you send and leaves the rest. `rules` replaces the whole rule set.
Only the shelf's owner or an admin can change it, and the Wishlist shelf can't be
changed at all.

403.description: The shelf is someone else's, or it is the Wishlist shelf.

404.description: No shelf has that id, or it is another reader's private shelf.

409.description: You already have a shelf with that name.

422.description: A field is invalid, or the change would give a hand-picked shelf rules or leave a smart shelf with none; the body says which.

post.description:
Appends books to a hand-picked shelf. A book already on it stays where it is. Every
uuid must match a book, or nothing is added. Only the shelf's owner or an admin can
add books, and the Wishlist shelf can't be edited this way.

204.description: The books are on the shelf.

403.description: The shelf is someone else's, or it is the Wishlist shelf.

404.description: No shelf has that id, it is another reader's private shelf, or a uuid matches no book.

422.description: More than 2000 uuids, or a uuid longer than 64 bytes.

delete.summary: Remove a book from a shelf
delete.description:
Takes the book off a hand-picked shelf. Removing a book that isn't on the shelf, or an
unknown uuid, still succeeds. Only the shelf's owner or an admin can remove books, and
the Wishlist shelf can't be edited this way.

204.description: The book is off the shelf.

403.description: The shelf is someone else's, or it is the Wishlist shelf.

404.description: No shelf has that id, or it is another reader's private shelf.

get.description:
The books on a shelf, narrowed by `filter`. A smart shelf lists them in the order
`sort` and `dir` ask for; a hand-picked shelf lists them in the order they were added.
There is no paging: the list stops at 50,000 books.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
The order to list a smart shelf's books in. Defaults to `recently_interacted`, as
does a value the server doesn't know. A hand-picked shelf keeps its own order.

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description:
`asc` or `desc`. Any other value, or none, means `desc`. A hand-picked shelf
ignores it.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
Filter clauses as a percent-encoded JSON array, in the same form as `filter` on
`GET /api/ebooks`.

400.description: `filter` is malformed.

404.description: No shelf has that id, or it is another reader's private shelf.

422.description: A rule on the smart shelf holds a value that can't be evaluated, such as a year that isn't a number.

get.description:
The outgoing mail server Send to Kindle uses, with the password left out. Needs an
admin account.

post.description: Sets the outgoing mail server Send to Kindle uses. Needs an admin account.

200.description: The settings are saved; the body is what is now set.

422.description: `host` is empty or over 255 bytes, `port` is 0, `username` is over 255 bytes, `password` is over 1024 bytes, or `from_email` isn't an email address; the body says which.

post.description: Removes the saved outgoing mail server. Needs an admin account.

200.description: The settings are cleared; the body is what is now set.

post.description:
Emails a short message, with no book attached, to your own Kindle address through the
saved mail server, and waits for the server to accept it. Needs an admin account.

200.description: The mail server accepted the test email.

409.description: The server has no email delivery set up.

422.description: You have no Kindle address set.

502.description: The mail server refused the email or didn't answer within 90 seconds.

get.description:
The cover of one suggested book. A suggestion's `cover_url` points here when it has a
cover.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The uuid of the book the suggestion is for.

404.description: No cover is stored for that book and rank.

get.description:
The providers to ask for a summary, in the order to ask them: Hardcover when the server
has a Hardcover key, then Google Books, then Open Library only when the server has
neither a Hardcover nor a Google Books key.

200.description: The sources, first to ask first.

get.description:
Every tag on a book, with the number of books carrying it, most-used first. Stops at
the 500 most-used tags.

The cover as a WebP thumbnail, `sm` (160×240), `md` (320×480) or `lg` (640×960). A
thumbnail is made on first request: until it is ready, which takes seconds, the full
cover stands in for it, marked to be cached for only a few seconds.

200.description: The thumbnail, or the full cover while the thumbnail is being made.

202.description: The book has no cover, so there is no thumbnail to make.

304.description: The image is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`.

400.description: `size` is not `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

get.description:
Any user's profile picture, for drawing beside their name. By default a WebP thumbnail
at most 160 pixels on its longest edge; `size=full` gets the image as uploaded. The URL
stays the same when the user replaces their avatar, so revalidate with `If-None-Match`.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description:
`full` for the image as uploaded. Anything else, or leaving it out, gets a WebP
thumbnail at most 160 pixels on its longest edge.

304.description: The avatar is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`.

404.description: No user has that id, or the user has no avatar.

book_uuids.description: The uuids of the books to add, up to 2000.

AddPhysicalOnlyRequest.description:
Add a physical-only book (not in the library) from resolved external meta —
creates a fileless book plus its first physical copy.

AdminHealthReport.description:
Full report backing `/admin/health`'s five sections, returned in one
request by `GET /api/admin/health` (REST) / `rpc_get_admin_health`
(web). The web page re-fetches this on a 5-second live-update poll
in addition to its initial page-load fetch.

AdminUserRow.description:
Admin Users-table projection of a `users` row. Extends
[`UserSummary`] with the created timestamp and locked state the admin
table renders, without bloating the login-path summary. No password
fields ever cross the wire.

display_name.description: Presentation name, or `None` when the user hasn't set one.

locked.description:
`true` when the account is currently locked out by repeated failed
logins (`locked_until` is in the future).

ApiTokenView.description:
One live API token in the management listing (`GET /api/auth/api-tokens`).
Never carries the secret — that appears exactly once, in
[`CreateApiTokenResponse::secret`].

last_used_at.description: `None` until the token first authenticates a request.

suffix.description:
Last 4 characters of the raw token, for the `omni_…xxxx` display
identifier. `None` on tokens minted before the suffix was recorded.

AuthorDetail.description:
Author detail payload for `GET /api/authors/:id` and `rpc_get_author`.
Contains the author row plus every book by that author.

has_photo.description: `true` when a usable profile photo is cached for this author (a `manual` or `openlibrary` row in `author_photos`). The frontend hero swaps the letter avatar for `` when set. `'letter'` negative-cache rows do not set this flag.

reading.description:
The caller's state on each of `books` they have opened or marked;
a book absent here is unread with no position.

AuthorPhotoScanResult.description:
Result of an admin-triggered "Scan for picture" run. The endpoint
clears any cached row and runs the Open Library cascade inline; a
`false` here means Open Library had nothing to offer for this author
and a sticky `letter` marker has been written to skip future
autoresolution.

url.description: An `http` or `https` URL of a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image, up to 2048 bytes.

AuthorReading.description:
One reader's progress through one author's books, for the `/authors`
list. Per-reader, so it rides its own request beside [`AuthorSummary`],
which every reader shares. An author the reader never opened is absent.

last_read_at.description: The newest [`BookReading::last_read_at`] across the author's books.

AuthorSummary.description:
Lightweight author row for the `/authors` index. Carries only what the
card needs — no joined book list. The detail page (`AuthorDetail`) is
fetched on click.

accent.description:
Cover-derived accent color borrowed from the author's first book
with a non-null `accent_color`. `None` when no owned book has one
— the UI falls back to the theme accent.

has_photo.description: `true` when a usable profile photo is cached for this author (a `manual` or `openlibrary` row in `author_photos`). Same semantics as `AuthorDetail::has_photo` — `'letter'` negative-cache rows do not set this flag. Lets the `/authors` index render a real `` in one round trip instead of fetching the detail payload per card.

BookDeletionImpact.description:
What a total delete would take with the book — the numbers the confirm
dialog names before an admin commits.

BookDeletionManifest.description:
Everything the delete dialog needs for one book: the deletable items and
the user data a total delete would take with them.

BookFileInfo.description:
One `book_files` row — a single physical file on disk. Exposed to the
frontend so the format switcher can offer a file picker when N > 1.

duration_seconds.description:
Playing time of this file, summed over its parts. Present for audio rows only,
so never guess an audiobook's runtime from elsewhere.

Whole seconds, unlike the fractional `ProgressRecord::total_duration_seconds`:
a catalog row is read for "how long is it", not for position arithmetic.

etag.description:
Content validator for this file (see [`crate::file_etag`]). An offline client
snapshots it at download time and compares it with a later metadata refresh to
learn its copy is stale. `None` for rows the scanner has not stat'd yet, so the
one-time backfill never reads as a content change.

path.description:
Library-relative path (`book_files.scan_key`, e.g.
`clarke/piranesi.epub`) — what the delete dialog shows so an admin can
see exactly which file on disk a row stands for. `None` for rows
predating the `scan_key` backfill.

size_bytes.description:
On-disk size of this file. Lets the per-file Send-to-Kindle rows gate
oversized EPUBs the same way the hero export menu does.

BookReading.description:
One reader's state on one book: its status, how far in, and when.
`status` is the stored one; a book with a position but no stored status
reads as `Reading`, as it does on the Continue rail.

oneOf.description:
The latest position's format and audio file, so a Resume opens the
reader or player (and file) it was left in. `None` without a position.

last_read_at.description:
Unix seconds of the latest position (client time), else of the status
change; `None` for a book marked `Unread`.

percent.description: Whole-book percent of the latest position, floored; `None` without one.

BookRef.description: The uuid of the book a check-in / add / wishlist write landed on.

BookSuggestion.description:
One suggested read-alike from Hardcover. External to the library — clicking
opens `hardcover_url` in a new tab.

cover_url.description:
Relative URL to the cached cover (`/api/suggestions/:uuid/:rank/cover`),
or `None` when no cover was cached (the UI falls back to a typographic
plate). Clients combine it with their configured server base.

list_count.description:
Co-listing count — how many curated Hardcover lists co-shelve this book
with the source book. The relevance signal shown as "on N lists".

book_uuid.description:
The book uuid the event named, if any (a `book_uuid` or `uuid`
field), letting the UI link straight to `/books/{uuid}`.

file.description:
The file path the event named, if any (a `file`, `path`, or
`file_path` field).

message.description: The event's `message` field, or empty when it carried none.

target.description: Event target — the emitting module path.

timestamp.description: Unix-seconds timestamp when the event was captured.

CheckInRequest.description: Check in a physical copy of a book already in the library.

Contributor.description:
A contributor (or creator) with the optional OPF refinements: the MARC role
code (`aut`, `ill`, `edt`, `bkp`, `trl`, …) and the sort-key name.

`id` is the `authors.id` primary key, set when loaded from a m2m join and
`None` for contributors created by the EPUB parser before indexing.

CreateApiTokenResponse.description:
Response from `POST /api/auth/api-tokens`. `secret` is the raw `omni_…`
token, shown to the client exactly once — the server keeps only its hash,
so it is unrecoverable afterward. Deliberately does not derive `Debug`,
same as `LoginRequest`: a stray `tracing::debug!(?resp)` must not leak a
long-lived credential.

CreateShelfRequest.description:
Create payload. For smart: `match_mode` + `rules` set, `book_uuids` empty.
For manual: `match_mode`/`rules` empty, `book_uuids` optional.

CreateUserRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/admin/users` (admin create). See
[`LoginRequest`] for why `Debug` is deliberately not derived.

DeleteBookFilesRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/books/{uuid}/delete-files`: the `book_files`
ids and physical-copy ids to remove. Either list may be empty; both empty
on a book with no items at all deletes the record.

book_deleted.description:
True when the book row itself was removed, so the caller must navigate
away instead of refetching a page that no longer exists.

DeviceView.description:
A registered device row as shown to its owner or an admin. Shared by the
admin `GET /api/admin/users/{id}/devices` listing (self-service devices
are deferred — see `/api/auth/devices` note in the PR body).

total.description:
Total FTS5 hit count *before* the server-side `MAX_BOOKS_RETURNED` cap,
set by the search paths so the web client can show "N of M results"
even when `books` is truncated. `None` for the full-library
(`/api/ebooks`, `rpc_get_ebooks`) responses, which surface truncation
via the `X-Total-Count` header instead.

EbookMetadata.description:
Parsed metadata for a single ebook file.

`cover_url` is a relative URL to `/api/covers/:id` when the book has a cover;
clients combine it with their configured server base. OPF
`<dc:contributor>` entries are merged into `creators` (creators first).

accent.description:
Cover-derived accent color. Opaque CSS color value extracted
during indexing. `None` means "no cover or extraction failed" —
the frontend falls back to the theme default accent.

added_at.description:
Row insertion timestamp from `books.timestamp` — SQLite
`datetime('now')` format (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, UTC, space separator).
Drives the "Newest Added" sort — distinct from `modified` (DC
last-write).

book_files.description:
Every `book_files` row on this book, one per file on disk, including ordinary
single-file books. Each row carries that file's content validator
(`BookFileInfo::etag`) for offline staleness checks; count rows per format
rather than reading emptiness as a proxy. Empty only on the list projection,
which does not join this table.

description.description:
Sanitized HTML. `None` on browse rows — `LibraryPage.books`, their stack
members, and keyset `/api/ebooks` pages sent `omit_description=true` —
which never carry it: absent there is not empty, so read the book's
detail for it.

epub_size_bytes.description:
On-disk size of the file the hero "Send to Kindle" would deliver (the
lowest-ordinal EPUB, else the PDF). `None` when the book has neither.
Drives the oversized-file gate on the email button — see
`kindle_email_oversize`.

genres.description:
User-assigned genres. Unlike `subjects` (which the EPUB OPF supplies
via `<dc:subject>`), no file format Omnibus reads carries a genre, so
this list is sourced entirely from `metadata_overrides` — there is no
scanned baseline to revert to and no canonical link table behind it.

has_cover_override.description: True when `cover_url` is a user-uploaded override cover, not the scanned original.

has_override.description:
True when user-supplied metadata overrides are active for this book.
The detail page uses this to show a "has overrides" indicator and
offer a revert action.

has_physical.description: Whether the book has ≥1 physical copy checked in (drives the physical badge).

isbn10.description:
Secondary ISBN-10, sourced entirely from `metadata_overrides` — no
file format Omnibus reads carries a distinct ISBN-10 alongside its
ISBN-13, so unlike `isbn13` there is no scanned baseline underneath
this one.

isbn13.description:
Primary ISBN-13: derived from whichever `identifiers` entry (in
DB-projection order, not original OPF scan order) has a scheme
mentioning "isbn" and a value that normalizes to 13 ASCII digits, or
a user override from `metadata_overrides` layered on top at read
time. `None` when neither source has one.

last_interacted_at.description:
Most recent moment *anyone* interacted with the book — rated it,
published a journal entry, changed its read status, added it to the
library, edited its metadata or cover, or checked in a physical copy.
Fixed-width ISO, so it sorts lexicographically. Drives the "Recently
Interacted" sort; `None` only for a book carrying no signal at all.

page_count.description:
Page count of the CBZ archive `/api/ebooks/{uuid}/pages/{n}` would
serve, so the comic pager can render a slider and map progress onto
page indices. `None` for an EPUB-only book, a malformed archive, or
a row not yet backfilled since being indexed.

print_pages.description:
User-supplied print edition page count, sourced entirely from
`metadata_overrides`. Distinct from `page_count`, the CBZ archive's *image*
count that drives a comic's page slider: this is bibliographic metadata about
a print edition and can coexist with it.

series_id.description:
Stable `series.id` primary key from the normalized DB. Set when the
book was loaded from a join; `None` for books not in any series.

unique_identifier.description:
OPF unique identifier (`<dc:identifier id="…">`). Used by the
frontend to construct `/books/:uuid` and `/api/covers/:uuid` URLs.

stacks.description:
The series folded into one row each. Absent unless the request set `stack_series`
and the page held a series of two or more books.

EbookPage.description:
One response of `GET /api/ebooks`: a page of books, plus the series it folded into
stacks when the request set `stack_series`.

EditionHydrateRequest.description:
Body for `POST /api/metadata/editions/hydrate`, the second call the picker
makes once a candidate is selected, naming one edition rather than a query.

`provider_ref` is echoed back exactly as the search handed it over; Omnibus
never parses it, so it is capped rather than validated for shape.

isbn13.description:
The candidate's ISBN-13, when it has one.

Optional because a candidate may have none; `provider_ref` is the re-fetch
handle. When present it is still preferred, since it names a *printing*
where a bare handle may name a work.

isbn.description:
An ISBN the caller already holds for this book, in any format — it is
normalized (and a bad one discarded) server-side.

The strongest signal there is, and the one the old flat query threw
away even when the edit form had it sitting in a field.

providers.description:
Which providers to ask. Absent means every configured one; this is the
hook a provider-filter UI plugs into without a wire change.

query.description:
The query as free text — what the reader sees in the search box, and
the whole request from a client that sends nothing else.

title.description:
The book's title on its own, when the caller can separate it. Lets each
provider be asked in *its* terms: Open Library searches the author's name
inside the title field if handed one flattened string. Absent means "the
reader typed something specific": treat [`Self::query`] as the title, with
no author.

EditionSearchResponse.description:
Fan-out search results: the candidates every asked provider returned, plus
one status row per provider considered — including the ones that were
skipped or failed, which is why a caller can render "Hardcover: couldn't
reach it" instead of quietly showing a shorter list.

ExternalBookMeta.description:
Normalized book metadata resolved from an external provider. Every field but
`isbn13`, `title`, and `source` is best-effort — providers disagree on which
they carry. `cover_url` is a provider-hosted image the caller fetches only
when a book/wishlist entry is actually created, not at lookup time.

first_publish_year.description:
Year the *work* was first published, across all editions — distinct
from `year`, which is this edition's own date.

isbn13.description: The normalized ISBN-13 that resolved (always 13 digits, no hyphens).

series.description:
Series statement as the provider reports it (free text, e.g.
"The Kingkiller Chronicle (1)"). Best-effort Open Library enrichment.

year.description: Publication year or date as the provider reports it (free text).

FileBytes.description:
A file's raw bytes, such as an image, an EPUB or an audio part. Never JSON: the
operation's content type says what the bytes are.

FtsHealth.description:
`books_fts` vs `books` row-count parity. A rebuild
(`POST /api/fts/rebuild`) always restores `in_sync`; drift here means a
post-commit FTS update failed silently on some earlier write.

GenreWeight.description:
One genre with the number of books carrying it. Structurally a
[`TagWeight`], kept a distinct type so `/api/genres` and `/api/tags`
don't share a wire name for two different vocabularies.

GoogleBooksKeyStatus.description:
Masked status of the server-wide Google Books key for the Settings UI.
**Never carries the raw key** — only a short masked preview. Mirrors
[`crate::suggestion::HardcoverKeyStatus`].

masked.description: Short masked preview (e.g. `AIza…9f3a`), or `None` when unset.

source.description: Where the effective key comes from: `"settings"`, `"env"`, or `"none"`.

HardcoverKeyStatus.description:
Masked status of the server-wide Hardcover key for the Settings UI. **Never
carries the raw key** — only a short masked preview.

masked.description: Short masked preview (e.g. `hc_l…3f9a`), or `None` when unset.

source.description: Where the effective key comes from: `"settings"`, `"env"`, or `"none"`.

Health.description: A running server's liveness and build details.

app.description: Always `omnibus`, which tells this server apart from another program on the port.

build_id.description:
When this server process started, in Unix milliseconds. It changes on every restart,
so a new value means a rebuilt server is up.

repo_root.description:
The directory the server runs from. Development tooling uses it to tell the servers of
two checkouts apart.

time.description: The server's clock in Unix seconds, so a client can measure how far its own clock is off.

version.description: The release, such as `v0.9.3`, or `dev` for a local build.

Identifier.description: A typed identifier from the OPF, e.g. `{ scheme: "ISBN", value: "…" }`.

IndexStatus.description: Library index summary: configured library paths and row counts.

KindleSendQueued.description: A Send to Kindle that is queued to go out.

task_id.description: Pass this to `GET /api/kindle/send/status` to follow the send.

KindleSendRequest.description: The book to email to your Kindle address.

book_uuid.description: The book's uuid, at most 64 bytes.

file_id.description:
The `id` of one of the book's `book_files`, for a book with several. Leave it out to
send the book's EPUB, or its PDF when it has no EPUB.

KindleSendStatus.description:
Terminal-or-pending status of a Send-to-Kindle job, returned by the
`kindle/send/status` poll endpoint keyed on the `task_id` that the enqueue
call handed back. The send runs on the background worker; the client posts
once, then polls this until it flips off `Pending`. `Failed.message` is the
per-case reason surfaced to the button toast.

LoginRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/auth/login`.

Deliberately does not derive `Debug`: the struct holds a plaintext
password, and a stray `tracing::debug!(?req)` would write it to logs.

client_kind.description:
Optional — when present, server issues a bearer session instead of a
cookie session and includes the raw token in the response.

LoginResponse.description:
Response from `POST /api/auth/login` and `POST /api/auth/register`.
`token` is populated only for bearer (mobile) sessions; cookie sessions
return the cookie in a `Set-Cookie` header and `token` is `None`.

MatchMode.description: How smart conditions combine: `Any` = OR, `All` = AND.

McpStatus.description:
Whether the hosted `/mcp` endpoint is enabled; the body of
`GET`/`POST /api/settings/mcp` and the matching rpc pair. Mirrors
`RegistrationStatus`'s shape for the other instance-level switch.

MergeBooksRequest.description: Request body for `POST /api/books/merge`: merge the source book into the target.

MergeBooksResult.description:
Result of a successful merge: the audit-log id (the undo handle) and
the surviving book's uuid.

MetadataProvider.description: Which external provider a lookup resolved against.

PhysicalCopy.description:
A physical copy of a book, seen library-wide (shared by all users like a
digital file) but changed only by the reader who filed it — see
[`Self::can_change`]. A book can have many; each is individually deletable.

added_by_name.description:
That user's display name (username when unset), for "checked in by".
`None` when the account is gone or on a payload a client built itself.

added_by_user_id.description: User who checked the copy in; `None` if that account was later deleted.

checked_in_at_iso.description:
[`Self::checked_in_at`] rendered as ISO 8601 UTC. When the copy was checked in.

`None` on a payload a client built itself.

isbn.description: Scanned ISBN for this copy; `None` for a manual (non-scan) add.

note.description: Free-text edition/publisher note until an edition-metadata provider exists.

ProgressFormat.description:
Discriminator for the format-specific payload variant in [`ProgressUpdate`]
/ [`ProgressRecord`] / [`SessionReport`]. Serializes as a plain
lowercase string (`"epub"` / `"audio"`) so the wire shape stays compact.

ProviderCapabilities.description:
What one provider can be asked and what it can return, independent of
whether it is currently configured. A flag is a claim about the provider's
API, not one book: flip one only in the same change that teaches the
provider module to parse the field onto [`ProviderEdition`], because a
fixture cross-check fails a flag that outruns its parser.

ProviderEdition.description:
One candidate from one provider in a fan-out edition search, kept
**attributed and un-collapsed**: two editions sharing an ISBN across two
sources stay two entries, because telling editions apart is what the picker
is for. A separate type from [`ExternalBookMeta`], the frozen check-in wire
payload; convert with `TryFrom` where a check-in-shaped value is wanted.

first_publish_year.description:
Year the *work* was first published, across all editions — distinct
from `year`, which is this edition's own date.

genres.description:
Genres as this provider labels them, already sanitized and capped at
[`Self::MAX_GENRES`].

Empty means "this provider has none for this book"; whether a source can
answer for genres *at all* is [`ProviderCapabilities::carries_genres`].

isbn10.description:
ISBN-10 for the **same** printing as [`Self::isbn13`], when the provider
carries one. Only set when the two demonstrably name one edition, since
providers list identifiers per *work* as readily as per edition. `None` is
the normal answer for a 979-prefixed ISBN-13, which has no ISBN-10.

isbn13.description:
The normalized ISBN-13 (13 digits, no hyphens), when the provider ties one
to *this* edition. Optional on purpose: a search hit is often a *work*, not a
printing, so a candidate needs a [`Self::provider_ref`] to be re-fetched by,
not an ISBN. The check-in path still requires one (see [`ExternalBookMeta`]).

pages.description:
The edition's **printed** length, which is what the `print_pages`
override stores — never `books.page_count`, which is a comic's image
count. `None` when the provider doesn't say; a provider reporting `0`
for "unknown" is normalized to `None` rather than staged over a real
page count.

provider_ref.description:
Opaque, provider-scoped handle for re-fetching this candidate in full once
it is selected, since a thin search hit carries less than the provider's own
record. Omnibus never parses it: it is the provider's own id where one
exists, else `isbn:<isbn13>`, which every provider can be re-queried by.

relevance.description:
How strongly this candidate matches the query that found it, in
**hundredths of a point** (so `1000` is a perfect title match), or `None`
from a source that did not score. Derived from the candidate and the query
alone, never from which provider answered, so a source dropping out removes
its rows and reorders nothing.

series_index.description:
This book's position in [`Self::series`], formatted for display
(`"1"`, `"2.5"`), or `None` when the provider doesn't say.

Only Hardcover models a series position, so the *other* providers
always leave this `None` — the same asymmetry `series` itself has.

year.description: Publication year or date as the provider reports it (free text).

ProviderInfo.description:
One entry in the provider catalog, built by `providers::catalog` in
`omnibus-db` and served by `GET /api/metadata/providers`.

**Never carries key material** — `configured` is a bool, not a masked
preview, because this endpoint is reachable by any authenticated user.

configured.description:
Whether the ladder would actually invoke this provider right now —
always `true` for a keyless-capable provider, key-gated otherwise.
Mirrors the same check `providers::ladder` uses, so the two can never
disagree about what "configured" means.

requires_key.description:
Whether an API key is required to reach this provider at all (as
opposed to optional — present or not, the provider still answers).

ProviderSearchSource.description: One row of the per-source status table returned alongside the candidates.

oneOf.description:
The provider answered. `count` is how many of its candidates reached
the returned list — post-cap, so it never overstates what is there.
Not usable on this instance (no API key). No request was sent.

Asked, but no answer came back. `message` is the provider call's own
top-level context, never the error chain below it — which is where a
request URL, and so a `?key=`, would render.

Skipped without a request: this provider rate-limited us recently and is
still inside its cooldown.

Distinct from [`Self::Failed`]: nothing was asked, and `retry_after_secs`
says when it is worth asking again.

retry_after_secs.description: Whole seconds left on the cooldown, rounded up.

ProviderSearchStatus.description:
What one provider contributed to a fan-out search.

The three cases are the point of the type: "it has nothing", "we never
asked it", and "we asked and never got an answer" are different facts, and
collapsing them makes an outage read as a miss.

ReadStatus.description:
A book's read-lifecycle state for one user. Serializes as a plain lowercase
string (`"unread"` / `"reading"` / `"finished"`) matching the
`book_read_status.status` CHECK constraint.

RegisterRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/auth/register`. See [`LoginRequest`] for
why `Debug` is deliberately not derived.

RegistrationStatus.description:
Whether self-registration is open; the body of `GET /api/auth/registration`
and `POST /api/settings/registration`.

RenameApiTokenRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /api/auth/api-tokens/{id}` — the row's Rename action.

ResolveMetaRequest.description:
Resolve a picked title-search candidate against the library — the ladder's
library rungs applied to metadata already in hand, so no provider round
trip (which could miss on an ISBN the search itself just surfaced).

RuleField.description:
A field a smart rule can match on. Mirrors the advanced-search query vocabulary plus
the acquisition-date fields.

RuleOp.description: A comparison operator for a smart rule.

RulePreview.description: Live-preview result for the create modal: "N of M match" + sample covers.

RulePreviewRequest.description: Unsaved rule sent to the preview endpoint.

ScanBook.description:
A library book matched during scan resolution — just enough to display and
act on it (the confirm/decision screens).

has_files.description:
Whether the book has a digital file. `false` for a paper-only or
wishlist-only book, whose confirm screen must not claim the reader
"already has this one digitally". Defaulted so a payload from before
the field decodes; nothing before it emitted the flag.

has_physical.description: Whether the book already has ≥1 physical copy checked in.

isbn.description:
The book's own ISBN identifier, separator-stripped. Lets the close-match
confirm show the library edition's ISBN beside the scanned one.

oneOf.description: Exact identifier hit; the book already has a physical copy.

Exact identifier hit; on the caller's physical wishlist (no physical
copy yet). The book they wanted and now hold, so clients offer to check
the copy in, which clears the entry.
Exact identifier hit; in the library digitally, no physical copy yet.

Online-resolved and (title, author)-matched at least one library book:
needs a human "is this the book?" confirmation before any write. Carried as
head + tail so the single-candidate wire shape stays byte-identical for older
clients; clients that know both render `book` followed by `others` as one
picker.
Online-resolved but not in the library.
Neither the library nor any provider knew the ISBN.

ScanOutcome.description:
Outcome of resolving a scanned/typed ISBN down the matching ladder. A fuzzy
(title, author) hit is a [`ScanOutcome::CloseMatch`] — never auto-resolved;
the client must confirm before any write, so a hit on several rows is a
picker rather than a reason to decline the match.

ScanSearchRequest.description:
Search the external providers by title text — the fallback offered when an
ISBN scan resolves to [`ScanOutcome::Unresolved`].

ScanSearchResponse.description:
Title-search results: provider-resolved candidates for the reader to pick
from, each complete enough to feed [`ResolveMetaRequest`].

SeriesDetail.description:
Series detail payload for `GET /api/series/:id` and `rpc_get_series`.
Books are ordered by `series_index`.

SeriesStack.description: A series folded into one grid tile.

lead_uuid.description: The member standing in the result list; the stack renders in its slot.

members.description: Every member in the result set, in series order.

series_id.description: The series page to link, when one resolves.

states.description: One state per member on server pages; empty on client-grouped stacks.

SeriesSummary.description:
Lightweight series row for the `/series` index. Carries the primary
author of the series (first book's first creator) so the card can
render the by-line without a second fetch.

accent.description: Accent color borrowed from the first book in the series with one.

primary_author.description:
Primary author display string (first book's first creator). `None`
when the series has no books with a linked author.

SessionView.description:
A session row as shown to its owner or an admin (device & session
management). Never exposes the token hash — only enough to
identify and revoke the row. Shared by the self-service
`GET /api/auth/sessions` and the admin `GET /api/admin/users/{id}/sessions`.

client.description:
Human-readable name of the client holding this session — the registered
device's name for a native client ("Seamus's iPhone"), otherwise a label
derived from the captured `User-Agent` ("Firefox on macOS"). Derived
server-side so the raw header never reaches a page; falls back to
[`UNKNOWN_CLIENT`] for a session minted before migration `0088`.

is_current.description:
`true` when this is the session the request authenticated with. Only set by
the self-service listing; the admin listing always returns `false`, even for
the admin's own session. Enforcement lives on the write side: the self-service
`DELETE /api/auth/sessions/{id}` refuses (400) to revoke the request's own
session id.

SetBookDetailScrollStops.description: Whether a book's detail page stops at each section as you scroll.

enabled.description: `true` stops at each section; `false` scrolls the page in one piece.

key.description:
The Google Books API key, up to 512 bytes. `null`, absent or blank clears the
saved key.

The Hardcover API token, up to 2048 bytes. `null`, absent or blank clears the
saved key.

SetHiddenFormats.description: The formats to hide from your library view.

formats.description:
Format names such as `cbz`, each 1 to 16 letters or digits, at most 32. Case and
duplicates don't matter. An empty or missing list hides nothing.

email.description:
The address books are emailed to, such as `name@kindle.com`. Null, missing or
blank clears it.

SetPasswordRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/admin/users/{id}/password` (admin password
reset). See [`LoginRequest`] for why `Debug` is deliberately not derived.

display_name.description:
The name other readers see, up to 64 characters with no control characters.
Null, missing or blank clears it, and your username shows instead.

SetShareStats.description: Whether other readers on this server can see your reading stats.

enabled.description: `true` shares your stats with the household; `false` keeps them to yourself.

SetStackSeries.description: Whether your library grid shows each series as one tile.

enabled.description: `true` folds a series into one tile; `false` shows every book on its own.

Settings.description:
User-configurable paths for the ebook and audiobook libraries, plus the
optional periodic-rescan cadence.

scan_interval_hours.description:
Hours between automatic rescans of both libraries. `None` disables periodic
scanning: the library then only reindexes on server boot or a manual "Scan
Library" click. Omitted from the wire payload when unset, so existing callers
see no change to the `Settings` JSON shape.

Shelf.description: Full shelf detail: the summary fields plus description, rule, and match mode.

owner_has_avatar.description:
Whether the owner has uploaded an avatar — see
[`ShelfSummary::owner_has_avatar`].

owner_username.description: Owner's username, for `by <name>` attribution on shelves you don't own.

sync_to_kobo.description:
Whether this shelf's books are exposed to the owner's Kobo devices over
wireless sync. Off by default — sync is never whole-library.

ShelfKind.description: Kind of shelf, fixed at creation.

ShelfPage.description: One page of a shelf's books (v1: capped, no cursor).

ShelfSummary.description: Compact shelf row for the rail: identity, kind, visibility, accent, count.

cover_uuids.description:
Up to four member book uuids (cover-bearing members first, shelf
default order) for gallery mosaic tiles. `default` keeps payloads from
older servers deserializable.

owner_has_avatar.description:
Whether the owner has uploaded an avatar, so attribution can draw
`GET /api/users/{owner_user_id}/avatar` instead of a monogram.
`default` keeps payloads from older servers deserializable.

owner_username.description: Owner's username, for `by <name>` attribution on shelves you don't own.

SmtpConfigStatus.description:
Masked status of the server-wide SMTP config for the Settings UI. **Never
carries the raw password** — only a short masked preview.

password_masked.description: Short masked preview of the password (e.g. `pa…rd`), or `None` when unset.

source.description: Where the effective config comes from: `"settings"`, `"env"`, or `"none"`.

SmtpConfigUpdate.description:
Admin request to save (or partially update) the server-wide SMTP config.

Deliberately does not derive `Debug`: it carries a plaintext SMTP password
that a stray `tracing::debug!(?req)` would log. `password` is `None` to leave
the stored password unchanged; a `Some("")` clears it.

SmtpSecurity.description: Transport security for the outbound SMTP connection.

SortDir.description: Ascending or descending sort direction for a [`SortKey`].

SortKey.description: Sortable axes exposed in the toolbar / table headers.

StackMemberState.description: The viewer's reading state for one member of a stack.

percent.description: Whole-book percent (0-100) from the ebook position, if any.

started.description: Opened in any format: a status, a percent, or a listening position.

StorageStats.description: Disk usage across the book library and every on-disk cache.

library_bytes.description:
Sum of `book_files.size_bytes` — the on-disk footprint of the
indexed library itself (not a cache, so it carries no cap).

oneOf.description: No Hardcover key is configured — the UI shows a connect message.
A resolution is enqueued and nothing is cached yet — the UI polls.

Cached results. `items` may be empty (sticky negative — Hardcover
matched nothing usable).

SuggestionsResponse.description: Response for a book's suggestions strip.

SummarySource.description: Which external provider a summary fetch should hit.

TagWeight.description: Single tag with its book count, for the tag cloud.

TaskKind.description:
Discriminant for [`TaskProgress`] entries. Mirrors the payload-less
shape of the server-side `Task` enum so the wire protocol stays
decoupled from the runtime `Task` type's lifetimes and handler
closures. `#[non_exhaustive]` so future worker actions can be added
without breaking client matches.

UndoMergeRequest.description: Request body for `POST /api/books/merge/undo`: the `merge_log` id to reverse.

UndoMergeResult.description: Result of a successful unmerge: the restored (source) book's uuid.

UpdateCopyNoteRequest.description:
Body of the copy-note edit (`PATCH /api/physical/copies/{id}`). `None` — and
any blank string — clears the note.

UpdateShelfRequest.description:
Partial update. `None` fields are left unchanged. `rules` replaces the whole
rule set (smart shelves only).

sync_to_kobo.description: Toggle the shelf's Kobo wireless-sync opt-in.

UserPermissions.description:
The four permission booleans that define what a user can do. `is_admin`
is presented in the UI as an "Administrator" permission that implies the
other three; the storage layer keeps them as independent flags (there is
no role enum). Used by the admin create/edit endpoints.

UserSummary.description: Safe projection of a `users` row. No password fields ever cross the wire.

book_detail_scroll_stops.description:
Whether this user's book detail page uses the snap-stop marquee.
`false` — the default, and what a pre-0092 payload decodes to —
renders it as one continuous scroll.

display_name.description:
Presentation name other users see, or `None` to fall back to
[`Self::username`] — which stays the login and admin identity.

has_avatar.description:
Whether this user has uploaded an avatar. Clients render
`GET /api/users/{id}/avatar` when set and a monogram otherwise.

hidden_formats.description:
Formats this user hides from the landing All Books view — canonical
lowercase tokens (`"cbz"`). Clients pass it back as the listing
request's `exclude_formats`; empty means nothing hidden.

kindle_email.description:
Send-to-Kindle destination address, or `None` when the user hasn't
configured one. Non-secret — the user set it themselves.

share_stats.description:
Whether other readers on this server may see this user's stats page.
`true` — the default, and what a pre-0099 payload decodes to.

stack_series.description: Whether this user's landing grid folds each series into one tile.

Visibility.description: Who can see a shelf. `Private` = owner + admins; `Public` = every user.

WishlistAddRequest.description:
Add a book to the caller's physical wishlist — either an existing library
book (`book_uuid`) or a new fileless book from external meta. Set one; if
both are present `book_uuid` wins and `meta` is ignored.

WishlistEntry.description: A book on one user's physical wishlist. Unique per `(user_id, book_uuid)`.

WishlistRemoval.description:
What removing a wishlist entry did beyond dropping the row. A book that
existed only to be wanted — no file, no copy, nobody else's wish — goes
with its last entry, and `book_deleted` is how the client learns the page
it is standing on is gone.

WishlistSource.description:
Where a wishlist entry was added from. Persisted as the `source` column.

The check-in flow has three front doors a reader tells apart: a barcode read
off the cover, an ISBN typed at the keypad, and a title search whose ISBN
came from the *provider* rather than the reader.

WorkerQueueEntry.description:
One [`TaskKind`]'s live queue depth and recent completion timings.
Timings are milliseconds (wire-friendly; the db-side `Worker::metrics`
uses `std::time::Duration`, which doesn't serialize), oldest first.

bearer.description: A session token from `POST /api/auth/login`, or an API token (`omni_…`) from `POST /api/auth/api-tokens`.

media_token.name: token
media_token.description: A bearer token passed in the URL, for media that an `` or `

session_cookie.name: __Host-omnibus_session
session_cookie.description: The cookie a browser sign-in sets. A server running without secure cookies (`OMNIBUS_SECURE_COOKIES=0`) names it `omnibus_session` instead.
